passages.text: “Be silent before Me, O islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come forward and testify; let us together draw near for judgment.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to all distant lands and nations.
He commands the islands to be silent before Him.
He tells the peoples to renew their strength.
He calls them to come forward.
He invites them to speak and testify.
He calls everyone to approach together for judgment.
passages.original: הַחֲרִ֤ישׁוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֔ים וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ יִגְּשׁוּ֙ אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה׃

passages.text: Who has aroused one from the east and called him to his feet in righteousness ? He hands nations over to him and subdues kings before him. He turns them to dust with his sword, to windblown chaff with his bow.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the one who acts with power and authority.
The LORD arouses a man from the east.
The LORD calls this man to stand in righteousness.
The LORD gives nations into this man's hand.
The LORD subdues kings before this man.
The LORD makes this man's sword turn kings to dust.
The LORD makes this man's bow scatter them like windblown chaff.
passages.original: מִ֤י הֵעִיר֙ מִמִּזְרָ֔ח צֶ֖דֶק יִקְרָאֵ֣הוּ לְרַגְל֑וֹ יִתֵּ֨ן לְפָנָ֤יו גּוֹיִם֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים יַ֔רְדְּ יִתֵּ֤ן כֶּֽעָפָר֙ חַרְבּ֔וֹ כְּקַ֥שׁ נִדָּ֖ף קַשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He pursues them, going on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet.
passages.sermon:
God calls a man from the east.
This man chases his enemies.
He moves forward in safety.
His feet barely touch the path.
passages.original: יִרְדְּפֵ֖ם יַעֲב֣וֹר שָׁל֑וֹם אֹ֥רַח בְּרַגְלָ֖יו לֹ֥א יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Who has performed this and carried it out, calling forth the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD—the first and the last— I am He.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD acts with power.
The LORD does great works.
The LORD calls each generation from the very beginning.
The LORD is the first.
The LORD is also the last.
The LORD alone is God.
passages.original: מִֽי־ פָעַ֣ל וְעָשָׂ֔ה קֹרֵ֥א הַדֹּר֖וֹת מֵרֹ֑אשׁ אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ רִאשׁ֔וֹן וְאֶת־ אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים אֲנִי־ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: The islands see and fear; the ends of the earth tremble. They approach and come forward.
passages.sermon:
The islands see.
The islands feel fear.
The ends of the earth tremble.
The ends of the earth feel afraid.
The islands and the ends of the earth come near.
They approach and come forward.
passages.original: רָא֤וּ אִיִּים֙ וְיִירָ֔אוּ קְצ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ קָרְב֖וּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן׃

passages.text: Each one helps the other and says to his brother, “Be strong!”
passages.sermon: Each person helps his neighbor.\r\nEach person says to his brother, “Be strong!”
passages.original: אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֖הוּ יַעְזֹ֑רוּ וּלְאָחִ֖יו יֹאמַ֥ר חֲזָֽק׃

passages.text: The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and he who wields the hammer cheers him who strikes the anvil, saying of the welding, “It is good.” He nails it down so it will not be toppled.
passages.sermon:
A craftsman encourages a goldsmith.
A man with a hammer cheers the one who strikes the anvil.
They look at the welding and say, "It is good."
They fasten it with nails.
They make sure it will not fall over.
passages.original: וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק חָרָשׁ֙ אֶת־ צֹרֵ֔ף מַחֲלִ֥יק פַּטִּ֖ישׁ אֶת־ ה֣וֹלֶם פָּ֑עַם אֹמֵ֤ר לַדֶּ֙בֶק֙ ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַיְחַזְּקֵ֥הוּ בְמַסְמְרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט׃ס

passages.text: “But you, O Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, descendant of Abraham My friend— I brought you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I said, ‘You are My servant.’ I have chosen and not rejected you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God calls Israel His servant.
God calls Jacob His servant.
God chose Jacob.
Jacob is a descendant of Abraham.
Abraham is God's friend.
God brought Israel from the ends of the earth.
God called Israel from the farthest places.
God said to Israel, "You are My servant."
God chose Israel.
God did not reject Israel.
passages.original: וְאַתָּה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדִּ֔י יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ זֶ֖רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹהֲבִֽי׃ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱזַקְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵאֲצִילֶ֖יהָ קְרָאתִ֑יךָ וָאֹ֤מַר לְךָ֙ עַבְדִּי־ אַ֔תָּה בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֥א מְאַסְתִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My right hand of righteousness.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel, His chosen servant.
God says, “Do not fear.
I am with you.
Do not be afraid.
I am your God.
I will make you strong.
I will help you.
I will hold you up with My right hand.
My right hand is righteous.”
passages.original: אַל־ תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י עִמְּךָ־ אָ֔נִי אַל־ תִּשְׁתָּ֖ע כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֣י אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אִמַּצְתִּ֙יךָ֙ אַף־ עֲזַרְתִּ֔יךָ אַף־ תְּמַכְתִּ֖יךָ בִּימִ֥ין צִדְקִֽי׃

passages.text: Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be reduced to nothing and will perish.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel, His chosen servant.
God says, “Look at your enemies.
All who are angry with you will feel shame.
All who oppose you will be disgraced.
Those who fight against you will become nothing.
Those who argue with you will disappear.
Your enemies will perish.”
passages.original: הֵ֤ן יֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ וְיִכָּ֣לְמ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל הַנֶּחֱרִ֣ים בָּ֑ךְ יִֽהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וְיֹאבְד֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י רִיבֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You will seek them but will not find them. Those who wage war against you will come to nothing.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God promises to protect them from their enemies.
You will look for your enemies.
You will not find them.
Those who attack you will disappear.
Those who fight against you will become nothing.
Your enemies will have no power over you.
passages.original: תְּבַקְשֵׁם֙ וְלֹ֣א תִמְצָאֵ֔ם אַנְשֵׁ֖י מַצֻּתֶ֑ךָ יִהְי֥וּ כְאַ֛יִן וּכְאֶ֖פֶס אַנְשֵׁ֥י מִלְחַמְתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and tells you: Do not fear, I will help you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD takes hold of your right hand.
The LORD says to you, "Do not fear."
The LORD says, "I will help you."
passages.original: כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מַחֲזִ֣יק יְמִינֶ֑ךָ הָאֹמֵ֥ר לְךָ֛ אַל־ תִּירָ֖א אֲנִ֥י עֲזַרְתִּֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Do not fear, O worm of Jacob, O few men of Israel. I will help you,” declares the LORD. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jacob and Israel.
Jacob and Israel are small and weak.
God calls Jacob a worm.
God calls Israel few in number.
God says, “Do not fear.”
God promises, “I will help you.”
The LORD declares this promise.
God is the Redeemer of Israel.
God is the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּֽירְאִי֙ תּוֹלַ֣עַת יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב מְתֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עֲזַרְתִּיךְ֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Behold, I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God promises to change Israel.
God will make Israel strong and effective.
God will make Israel like a new threshing sledge.
This sledge will be sharp.
This sledge will have many teeth.
Israel will thresh the mountains.
Israel will crush the mountains.
Israel will make the hills like chaff.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה שַׂמְתִּ֗יךְ לְמוֹרַג֙ חָר֣וּץ חָדָ֔שׁ בַּ֖עַל פִּֽיפִיּ֑וֹת תָּד֤וּשׁ הָרִים֙ וְתָדֹ֔ק וּגְבָע֖וֹת כַּמֹּ֥ץ תָּשִֽׂים׃

passages.text: You will winnow them, and a wind will carry them away; a gale will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God calls them few and weak.
God promises to help them.
God says, “You will winnow your enemies.”
A wind will carry your enemies away.
A strong storm will scatter them.
You will rejoice in the LORD.
You will praise the Holy One of Israel.
passages.original: תִּזְרֵם֙ וְר֣וּחַ תִּשָּׂאֵ֔ם וּסְעָרָ֖ה תָּפִ֣יץ אוֹתָ֑ם וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל בַּֽיהוָ֔ה בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּתְהַלָּֽל׃פ

passages.text: The poor and needy seek water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
passages.sermon:
The poor and needy look for water.
They cannot find any water.
Their tongues are dry from thirst.
I am the LORD.
I will answer them.
I am the God of Israel.
I will not leave them.
passages.original: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים מַ֙יִם֙ וָאַ֔יִן לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם בַּצָּמָ֣א נָשָׁ֑תָּה אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶעֱנֵ֔ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א אֶעֶזְבֵֽם׃

passages.text: I will open rivers on the barren heights, and fountains in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will open rivers on the barren heights.
The LORD will make fountains flow in the middle of the valleys.
The LORD will turn the desert into a pool of water.
The LORD will change the dry land into flowing springs.
passages.original: אֶפְתַּ֤ח עַל־ שְׁפָיִים֙ נְהָר֔וֹת וּבְת֥וֹךְ בְּקָע֖וֹת מַעְיָנ֑וֹת אָשִׂ֤ים מִדְבָּר֙ לַאֲגַם־ מַ֔יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִיָּ֖ה לְמוֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: I will plant cedars in the wilderness, acacias, myrtles, and olive trees. I will set cypresses in the desert, elms and boxwood together, so that all may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this and the Holy One of Israel has created it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Holy One of Israel.
The LORD will act with power.
The LORD will plant trees in the wilderness.
He will plant cedars there.
He will plant acacias there.
He will plant myrtles there.
He will plant olive trees there.
He will set cypresses in the desert.
He will set elms there.
He will set boxwood trees there.
He will put these trees together in the dry land.
People will see this work.
People will know what has happened.
People will think about it.
People will understand it together.
They will know the LORD’s hand has done this.
They will know the Holy One of Israel has created it.
passages.original: אֶתֵּ֤ן בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֶ֣רֶז שִׁטָּ֔ה וַהֲדַ֖ס וְעֵ֣ץ שָׁ֑מֶן אָשִׂ֣ים בָּעֲרָבָ֗ה בְּר֛וֹשׁ תִּדְהָ֥ר וּתְאַשּׁ֖וּר יַחְדָּֽו׃ לְמַ֧עַן יִרְא֣וּ וְיֵדְע֗וּ וְיָשִׂ֤ימוּ וְיַשְׂכִּ֙ילוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו כִּ֥י יַד־ יְהוָ֖ה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּ֑את וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרָאָֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: “Present your case,” says the LORD. “Submit your arguments,” says the King of Jacob.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD is also called the King of Jacob.
The LORD says, “Present your case.”
The King of Jacob says, “Submit your arguments.”
passages.original: קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם יֹאמַ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: “Let them come and tell us what will happen. Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome. Or announce to us what is coming.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to those who claim to have power.
God says, "Let them come."
Let them tell us what will happen.
Let them tell us about the things that happened before.
Then we can think about those things.
Then we can know what their end was.
Or let them tell us what will come next.
Let them announce the future to us.
passages.original: יַגִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּקְרֶ֑ינָה הָרִאשֹׁנ֣וֹת׀ מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה הַגִּ֜ידוּ וְנָשִׂ֤ימָה לִבֵּ֙נוּ֙ וְנֵדְעָ֣ה אַחֲרִיתָ֔ן א֥וֹ הַבָּא֖וֹת הַשְׁמִיעֻֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Tell us the things that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do something good or evil, that we may look on together in dismay.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to those who worship idols.
God challenges them to prove their power.
He says, “Tell us what will happen in the future.
Show us signs of what is coming next.
If you do this, we will know that you are gods.
Do something good or do something bad.
Let us see it together and be amazed.”
passages.original: הַגִּ֙ידוּ֙ הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת לְאָח֔וֹר וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם אַף־ תֵּיטִ֣יבוּ וְתָרֵ֔עוּ וְנִשְׁתָּ֖עָה וְנִרָא יַחְדָּֽו׃

passages.text: Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value. Anyone who chooses you is detestable.
passages.sermon: You are nothing.\r\nYour work has no value.\r\nAnyone who chooses you is detestable.
passages.original: הֵן־ אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן וּפָעָלְכֶ֖ם מֵאָ֑פַע תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה יִבְחַ֥ר בָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: I have raised up one from the north, and he has come— one from the east who calls on My name. He will march over rulers as if they were mortar, like a potter who treads the clay.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, “I have raised up a man from the north.
This man has come.
I have also called a man from the east.
This man calls on My name.
He will come against rulers.
He will crush them as if they were only mortar.
He will trample them like a potter treads clay.”
passages.original: הַעִיר֤וֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן֙ וַיַּ֔את מִמִּזְרַח־ שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֑י וְיָבֹ֤א סְגָנִים֙ כְּמוֹ־ חֹ֔מֶר וּכְמ֥וֹ יוֹצֵ֖ר יִרְמָס־ טִֽיט׃

passages.text: Who has declared this from the beginning, so that we may know, and from times past, so that we may say: ‘He was right’? No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.
passages.sermon:
No one declared these things from the beginning.
No one told us what would happen.
No one spoke so that we could know.
No one announced it in the past.
No one said, “He was right.”
No one foretold it.
No one heard your words.
No one listened to you.
No one gave us knowledge through your words.
passages.original: מִֽי־ הִגִּ֤יד מֵרֹאשׁ֙ וְנֵדָ֔עָה וּמִלְּפָנִ֖ים וְנֹאמַ֣ר צַדִּ֑יק אַ֣ף אֵין־ מַגִּ֗יד אַ֚ף אֵ֣ין מַשְׁמִ֔יעַ אַ֥ף אֵין־ שֹׁמֵ֖עַ אִמְרֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: I was the first to tell Zion: ‘Look, here they are!’ And I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God is the one who acts first.
God told Zion before anyone else.
God said to Zion, “Look, here they are.”
God gave Jerusalem a messenger.
This messenger brought good news.
passages.original: רִאשׁ֥וֹן לְצִיּ֖וֹן הִנֵּ֣ה הִנָּ֑ם וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר אֶתֵּֽן׃

passages.text: When I look, there is no one; there is no counselor among them; when I ask them, they have nothing to say.
passages.sermon:
God looks.
God sees no one present.
God finds no counselor among them.
God asks them questions.
They do not answer.
They have nothing to say.
passages.original: וְאֵ֙רֶא֙ וְאֵ֣ין אִ֔ישׁ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה וְאֵ֣ין יוֹעֵ֑ץ וְאֶשְׁאָלֵ֖ם וְיָשִׁ֥יבוּ דָבָֽר׃

passages.text: See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing; their images are as empty as the wind.
passages.sermon:
They are all a delusion.
Their works amount to nothing.
Their images are empty.
Their images are like the wind.
Their images have no substance.
